prompt: Complete ClassChainReporter, which walks up an object's class hierarchy with getClass() and getSuperclass(): depth counts the classes above it, chain names the whole line, and isKindOf searches it.
explanation: Every object can describe its own position in the class hierarchy: getClass() gives the exact runtime class and getSuperclass() steps one level up, returning null once you walk past java.lang.Object. A simple while loop over that chain is enough to count it, render it or search it. Integer sits two steps below Object because Number comes in between, which is the same relationship the compiler uses when it decides that an Integer is a Number.
hints: Use a Class<?> variable for the cursor and loop while it is not null, reassigning it to current.getSuperclass() each time.
depth counts only the classes ABOVE the object, so start the cursor at getClass().getSuperclass().
